items_missed: Never got the customer's name — the customer had to ask hers at the end ("and your name was?"), which means no name use anywhere in the call and no lead record to attach it to
Never captured an email address or phone follow-up, so a live inbound lead ended the call with zero capture — nothing to follow up on when his paperwork clears
No agenda statement and no "sound good?" — she jumped from the date question straight into pricing
No probe on access: 3rd-floor apartment and she never asked about elevator vs. stairs only, stairwell width, or parking proximity
No probe on walk distance despite the customer saying he is moving "from the front of the complex to the back" — this is the single biggest time driver on this move and it was never discussed
Never asked about the garage, patio/balcony, or storage areas; never asked about packing needs or box count
Never asked the moving-stressors question ("anything you're particularly worried about?")
No "pricing is super simple" opener and no full no-hidden-fees pitch (no credit card fee / no fuel surcharge / no assembly fee language)
No Worries Damage Coverage never explained — she said only "liability coverage" with no $2,000 figure and no 60¢/lb baseline contrast
Disassembly/reassembly-included never mentioned (customer described a bed frame, chest of drawers, and a bookshelf)
Clock-starts-on-site-when-the-contract-opens never explained; the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute proration were covered but with no sense-check after

No actual time estimate — she gave only the $620 minimum and a vague "usually a two bedroom apartment goes beyond the two and a half hour minimum," never a range, never stairs/walk-distance time impact
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing — no prep-equals-shorter-move framing, no consolidation examples, no take-a-carload tip
No attempt to book: Monday was available and she closed with "we'll be here if you need us" instead of asking to lock it in
No confirmation email offered, no "any other questions before I let you go," no hours or how to reach us
Rambling, hard-to-follow answer to the customer's 5:30pm question — the customer's assumption about our operating window was never clearly corrected
top_strength: She handled the money questions cleanly and honestly. When the customer floated a "two hour mark," she corrected it to policy without hedging — "we have a two and a half hour minimum, so any amount of time, even if it's like a one hour move it's still charged for two and a half hours" — then proactively volunteered "nothing is due ahead of time, we only collect once everything is actually completed for you, so there's no deposit." Her arithmetic was right and transparent: $192/hr, $48 per 15-minute increment, and a $620 all-in minimum with the $140 travel fee stated plainly as a one-time charge. She also checked real availability across Saturday, Sunday, Friday, and Monday rather than guessing.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: get the name and the email in the first ninety seconds, every call. This was a hot inbound lead — apartment paperwork pending, moving this week or next, already told her "you all popped up first" — and it ended with nothing captured. Open with "Absolutely, I can help with that — who do I have the pleasure of speaking with? And what's the best email for you? I'll get everything in writing so you have it when your keys come through." Second priority: she quoted a third-floor-down, front-of-complex-to-back-of-complex move without ever asking about the elevator, the stairwell, or the walk distance, which is a live estimate-accuracy risk — anchoring the customer on a $620 minimum when a 2BR third-floor carry with a long push realistically runs well past 2.5 hours sets up a sticker-shock invoice, exactly the pattern we are trying to close. Ask "is there an elevator or is it stairs only, and roughly how far is the walk from your door to where the truck can park?" then give a real range and name stairs and walk distance as the two variables. Third: zero differentiators landed — No Worries at $2,000, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee are the reasons a price-shopping caller stops shopping, and none of them were said. Also flagging: her answer to his 5:30pm question was too garbled to have corrected his belief that we are "closed and done by 5:30," so he may be planning around a start-time window we have not actually confirmed — worth a clear one-liner on latest start times.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and responsive with real affirmations ("Yeah, absolutely," "great question," "Absolutely, we'll be here if you need us") but transactional throughout — no name use at all, no empathy markers, and one answer confusing enough that the customer had to restate his question.
